questions.section: Part Two: Direct Questions [28 marks]
questions.question:
1.
  a) What is a magnet ? [4marks]
  b) What are the poles of magnet ? [4marks]
questions.answer_guide:
a) A magnet is a material or object that produces a magnetic field and attracts magnetic materials such as iron, nickel and cobalt.
b) The poles are the two ends of a magnet where the magnetic force is strongest – the north (N) pole and the south (S) pole. Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

2) Alternating current (AC) – changes direction periodically.

questions.section: Part Two: Direct Questions [28 marks]
questions.question: 3. Distinguish between transparent and translucent materials [4 marks]
questions.answer_guide: Transparent materials allow almost all light to pass through so objects can be seen clearly (e.g. clear glass, water). Translucent materials allow only part of the light through, scattering it, so objects are seen unclearly (e.g. frosted glass, tracing paper, oiled paper).

questions.section: Part Two: Direct Questions [28 marks]
questions.question: 4. List the five common properties of wave [4 marks]
questions.answer_guide: Reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference and polarization (also rectilinear propagation / dispersion).

questions.section: Part Two: Direct Questions [28 marks]
questions.question: 5. Compare with examples luminous and non – luminous bodies [4 marks]
questions.answer_guide: Luminous bodies produce their own light (e.g. the sun, stars, a candle flame, a lit bulb). Non-luminous bodies do not produce light; they are seen because they reflect light from a luminous source (e.g. the moon, a book, a table, people).

questions.section: Part Two: Direct Questions [28 marks]
questions.question: 6. Give reason why the red light is used as a universal danger signal ? [ 4 marks]
questions.answer_guide: Red light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum, so it is scattered least by air, fog, dust and smoke; it therefore travels farthest and can be seen clearly from a long distance.
